why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier's checks. Most of the builder brief is fine. Step 4 says to run `npm test`, which the criterion allows. Step 1 says a missing file should still throw, but it gives no actual command to run, so it doesn't copy the advisory's nonexistent-path command. Step 2 breaks the criterion. It says to write a test that "checks `loadConfig` on a file containing `{port: 9000` returns a value deep-equal to `{}`". That is the same input and expected output the verifier uses in Check 1 (`printf '{port: 9000' > "$d/bad.json"` … "The first output line is exactly `{}`"). The builder is allowed to write its own tests, but here the brief hands it the checker's exact test case, so the builder learns how it will be checked.
